## Natural history notes

A medium-sized day-flying sphinx moth characterized by a stout body, rapid hummingbird-like flight, dark brown wings with pale bands, and two bright yellow bands across the abdomen. In Florida, the Nessus Sphinx is found in gardens, forest edges, hammocks, fields, parks, and wooded neighborhoods where nectar flowers and grape-family host plants occur. Adults visit flowers during the day for nectar, while the caterpillars feed mainly on grape, Virginia creeper, and related vines, helping transfer vine growth into the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
